constitution.title: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, English text as amended
constitution.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
constitution.note: Arts. 48 and 50 (President elected by members of Parliament for five years), 59 (local government by elected bodies in every administrative unit), 65 (300 members from single territorial constituencies by direct election, plus 50 seats reserved for women elected by those members by proportional representation through single transferable vote), 72(3) (five-year Parliament), 123 (presidential elections 90 to 60 days before the term ends; general elections within 90 days before or after dissolution), and 142 (amendment).

rpo.title: The Representation of the People Order, 1972 (P.O. No. 155 of 1972)
rpo.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
rpo.note: The election law for Parliament: constituencies, nominations, polling, the count at each polling station, consolidation by the returning officer, and publication of results in the official Gazette.

rpo2026.title: Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 3 of 2026)
rpo2026.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
rpo2026.note: Amends P.O. No. 155 of 1972 with effect from 3 November 2025, the rules under which the 13th parliamentary election was held.

president_act.title: রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচন আইন, ১৯৯১ (Presidential Election Act, 1991)
president_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
president_act.note: The President is elected by members of Parliament under Art. 48; the Chief Election Commissioner is returning officer, and a sole valid nominee is declared elected without a poll.

referendum_act.title: গণভোট আইন, ১৯৯১ (Referendum Act, 1991)
referendum_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
referendum_act.note: Referendums on bills amending the provisions listed in Art. 142(1A), held by the Election Commission.

referendum_2025.title: গণভোট অধ্যাদেশ, ২০২৫ (Referendum Ordinance, 2025; Ordinance No. 67 of 2025)
referendum_2025.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
referendum_2025.note: Referendum on the constitutional reform proposals of the July National Charter 2025, polled on the day and during the hours of the 13th parliamentary election (s. 8); lapsed under Art. 93(2) after the poll.

women_seats.title: জাতীয় সংসদ (সংরক্ষিত মহিলা আসন) নির্বাচন আইন, ২০০৪ (Jatiya Sangsad Reserved Women's Seats Election Act, 2004)
women_seats.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
women_seats.note: Allocates the reserved women's seats to parties and alliances in proportion to their general seats and has the members of Parliament elect them.

delimitation.title: জাতীয় সংসদের নির্বাচনি এলাকার সীমানা নির্ধারণ আইন, ২০২১ (Delimitation of Parliamentary Constituencies Act, 2021)
delimitation.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
delimitation.note: The Election Commission delimits the 300 constituencies from the latest census, by administrative units, and publishes the list in the official Gazette.

up_act.title: স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) আইন, ২০০৯ (Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009; Act No. 61 of 2009)
up_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
up_act.note: s. 10(1): a union parishad of one chairman and 12 members, 9 for general seats (one per ward) and 3 for seats reserved for women; directly elected for five years.

up_2026.title: স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) (সংশোধন) আইন, ২০২৬ (Act No. 44 of 2026)
up_2026.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
up_2026.note: Amends the Union Parishad Act with effect from 1 September 2025.

upazila_act.title: উপজেলা পরিষদ আইন, ১৯৯৮ (Upazila Parishad Act, 1998; Act No. 24 of 1998)
upazila_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
upazila_act.note: An upazila parishad of a directly elected chairman and two vice-chairmen (one a woman), with the chairmen of the union parishads and mayors of the pourashavas in the upazila and reserved women members; five-year term.

pourashava_act.title: স্থানীয় সরকার (পৌরসভা) আইন, ২০০৯ (Local Government (Pourashava) Act, 2009; Act No. 58 of 2009)
pourashava_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
pourashava_act.note: A pourashava of a directly elected mayor, one councillor per ward, and councillors for seats reserved for women (a third of the wards); five-year term.

pourashava_2026.title: স্থানীয় সরকার (পৌরসভা) (সংশোধন) আইন, ২০২৬ (Act No. 60 of 2026)
pourashava_2026.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
pourashava_2026.note: Strikes clauses (55ক) and (61ক) of s. 2 and s. 20ক, the definitions and section added for party-nominated candidates, and adds ss. 32ক and 42ক (removal of mayors and councillors and appointment of administrators in special circumstances).

cc_act.title: স্থানীয় সরকার (সিটি কর্পোরেশন) আইন, ২০০৯ (Local Government (City Corporation) Act, 2009; Act No. 60 of 2009)
cc_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
cc_act.note: s. 5: a city corporation of a mayor, the councillors the government fixes by gazette notification, and seats reserved for women equal to a third of them; s. 6: five years from the first meeting.

zp_act.title: জেলা পরিষদ আইন, ২০০০ (Zila Parishad Act, 2000; Act No. 19 of 2000)
zp_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
zp_act.note: s. 4: a chairman, as many members as the district has upazilas, and women members a third of that number, all elected by the electoral college of s. 17 (the elected members of the city corporation, upazila parishads, pourashavas, and union parishads in the district); s. 5: five years from the first meeting.

hdc_act.title: রাংগামাটি পার্বত্য জেলা পরিষদ আইন, ১৯৮৯ (Rangamati Hill District Council Act, 1989)
hdc_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
hdc_act.note: A directly elected hill district council with seats by community; until an election the government forms an interim council of a chairman and 14 nominated members. The Khagrachhari and Bandarban acts of 1989 (Acts 20 and 21) are parallel.

chtrc_act.title: পার্বত্য চট্টগ্রাম আঞ্চলিক পরিষদ আইন, ১৯৯৮ (Chittagong Hill Tracts Regional Council Act, 1998)
chtrc_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
chtrc_act.note: A regional council over the three hill district councils, its chairman and members elected indirectly by the members of the hill district councils, with an interim council until that election.

cantonment_act.title: ক্যান্টনমেন্ট আইন, ২০১৮ (Cantonments Act, 2018)
cantonment_act.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
cantonment_act.note: Cantonment boards with members elected from the civilian wards of each cantonment alongside ex officio and nominated members.

gram_sarkar.title: গ্রাম সরকার আইন, ২০০৩ (Gram Sarkar Act, 2003)
gram_sarkar.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)
gram_sarkar.note: Village governments in each ward of a union, formed at a meeting of the ward's voters rather than by ballot.

gram_sarkar_repeal.title: গ্রাম সরকার (রহিতকরণ) আইন, ২০০৯ (Gram Sarkar (Repeal) Act, 2009)
gram_sarkar_repeal.publisher: Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Laws of Bangladesh)

portal.title: বাংলাদেশ জাতীয় তথ্য বাতায়ন (National Portal of Bangladesh), home page
portal.publisher: Cabinet Division and Aspire to Innovate (a2i), Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh
portal.note: The government's field-administration directory: links headed "৮ বিভাগ", "৬৪ জেলা", and "৫০২ উপজেলা", read on 2026-11-16. The Cabinet Division's page on divisions, districts, and upazilas points to these lists.

portal_unions.title: ইউনিয়নসমূহ (Unions), National Portal of Bangladesh
portal_unions.publisher: Cabinet Division and Aspire to Innovate (a2i), Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh
portal_unions.note: The directory of union offices embedded in the page: 4,568 records of office type union_portal (each with its division, district, and upazila), alongside 502 upazila, 64 district, and 8 division records, read on 2026-11-16.

lgd_achievements.title: অর্জন (Achievements), Local Government Division
lgd_achievements.publisher: Local Government Division, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives
lgd_achievements.note: Content last updated 7 November 2021: "বর্তমানে দেশের পৌরসভার সংখ্যা ৩২৮টি" (the country now has 328 pourashavas) and "স্থানীয় সরকার বিভাগের আওতাধীন ৬১টি জেলা পরিষদে" (the 61 zila parishads under the Division); also the five city corporations created since 2009 and the split of Dhaka into North and South.

portal_parliament.title: জাতীয় সংসদ (Jatiya Sangsad), National Portal of Bangladesh
portal_parliament.publisher: Cabinet Division and Aspire to Innovate (a2i), Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh
portal_parliament.note: 300 members, one per constituency by direct vote; reserved women's seats 15 in the first Parliament, none in the fourth, 30 in the others to the seventh, 45 from 2004, and 50 from the Fifteenth Amendment of 2011.

ecs.note: Administers every election in this census except party contests; publishes notifications, results by polling centre, and gazettes of returned candidates. classes.name: জাতীয় সংসদ নির্বাচন
classes.name_en: Jatiya Sangsad (Parliament) general elections: the 300 constituency seats
classes.note: 300 single-member territorial constituencies by plurality (Constitution Art. 65(2); RPO 1972). Parliament sits five years from its first meeting unless dissolved (Art. 72(3)), and the general election falls within 90 days before an expiry or after an early dissolution (Art. 123(3)). The Constituent Assembly of 1972 was made of members elected in Pakistan's 1970 elections and held no election of its own.
classes.locator: http://bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd/act-details-367.html (Art. 65(2): "Parliament shall consist of three hundred members to be elected in accordance with law from single territorial constituencies by direct election")

classes.note: A constituency seat that falls vacant is filled by a by-election within ninety days (Constitution Art. 123(4)) under the same rules as a general election.

classes.name_en: Reserved women's seats in Parliament, elected by the members
classes.note: 15 seats in the first Parliament, none in the fourth, 30 in the others to the seventh, 45 from 2004, and 50 since the Fifteenth Amendment of 2011, apportioned to parties and alliances by their general seats and elected by the 300 constituency members (Constitution Art. 65(3); Act of 2004). Parties usually file exactly their quota, so most seats are returned unopposed.

classes.note: The Fourth Amendment of 1975 made the presidency directly elected; elections were held on 3 June 1978, 15 November 1981, and 15 October 1986. The Twelfth Amendment, approved at the referendum of 15 September 1991, returned the choice to Parliament (class president_indirect).

A sole valid nominee is declared elected without a vote (Presidential Election Act 1991), as in most elections since 1991.

classes.name_en: Pourashava mayors (chairmen before 2009)
classes.note: A directly elected mayor for five years (Pourashava Act 2009); chairmen under the Paurashava Ordinance 1977 and earlier. Party nominations ran from the 2015 amendments until Act 60 of 2026 struck them.

classes.name_en: Pourashava councillors: ward seats and reserved women's seats
classes.note: One councillor per ward and reserved women's seats a third of the wards (Pourashava Act 2009); most pourashavas have nine wards and three reserved seats, so 12 contests per unit is a floor.

classes.name: সিটি কর্পোরেশন মেয়র নির্বাচন
classes.name_en: City corporation mayors
classes.note: A directly elected mayor for five years (City Corporation Act 2009, ss. 5 and 6). Dhaka, Chattogram, Khulna, and Rajshahi held the first direct mayoral polls in 1994; Barishal and Sylhet followed, then Narayanganj, Cumilla, Rangpur, Gazipur, and Mymensingh, and Dhaka was split into North and South in 2011. No count of corporations from an official register was reachable, so coverage has no unit total.

classes.name: ক্যান্টনমেন্ট বোর্ড নির্বাচন
classes.name_en: Elected civilian members of cantonment boards
classes.note: Each cantonment board has members elected from its civilian wards (Cantonments Act 2018).
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of cantonment board results or dates was found; the boards' own sites and the Election Commission's were not reachable from this environment.

classes.name: গ্রাম সরকার
classes.name_en: Village governments (gram sarkar), 2003-2009
classes.disposition_reason: Formed at meetings of each ward's voters, not by ballot, and abolished by the Gram Sarkar (Repeal) Act 2009.

classes.name: পূর্ব পাকিস্তান / পূর্ব বাংলা প্রাদেশিক পরিষদ ও পাকিস্তান জাতীয় পরিষদ
classes.name_en: Elections in East Bengal and East Pakistan before independence (1954 and 1970)
classes.disposition_reason: Held by Pakistan before independence, so they belong to Pakistan's census; the members elected in 1970 formed Bangladesh's Constituent Assembly without a further election.

classes.name: দলীয় মনোনয়ন
classes.name_en: Party nominations
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their candidates through their own boards; no state-run nominating contest exists.

classes.name: পেশাজীবী ও ছাত্র সংসদ নির্বাচন
classes.name_en: Bar councils, professional bodies, and university student unions
classes.disposition_reason: Elections of private or institutional electorates run by the bodies themselves, not public elections held by the Election Commission.
